subject: Polity
topic: Rajya Sabha — composition and powers — mixed tiers
description: Article 80, election, retirement cycle, special powers (249, 312), comparison with Lok Sabha

questions.stem: The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as per Article 80 is:
questions.explanation: Article 80(1)(a) — 12 members nominated by President from persons distinguished in literature, science, art and social service. Article 80(1)(b) — 238 representatives of States and UTs, indirectly elected. Total: 250. Current actual strength: 245 (since not all UTs send members yet). Lok Sabha max strength is 552 (530 from States + 20 from UTs + earlier 2 Anglo-Indian nominees, ended by 104th Amendment 2020).
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Rajya Sabha — composition and powers — mixed tiers

options.option_text: Elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, by single transferable vote

questions.explanation: Article 80(4) — RS members representing States are elected by ELECTED MEMBERS of the respective State Legislative Assembly using PROPORTIONAL REPRESENTATION (Single Transferable Vote — STV). UT representation similarly via members of UT Legislative Assembly or UT electoral college. Voting is by OPEN BALLOT (since 2003) — to prevent cross-voting. Each member's quota = (votes / (seats + 1)) + 1.

questions.stem: Rajya Sabha is a 'permanent' / 'continuous' chamber. The retirement pattern is:

options.option_text: 1/3 of members retire every 2 years; each member's term is 6 years

questions.explanation: Article 83(1) — RS is NOT subject to dissolution. Each member's term = 6 years. 1/3 retire every 2 years; new members elected to fill vacancies. Hence the chamber is 'continuous'. Lok Sabha (Article 83(2)) — 5-year term unless dissolved earlier. Original 5-year term came down to 6 from the original constitutional vagueness — the current 1/3 every 2 years pattern was set by Representation of the People Act, 1951.

questions.stem: Article 249 gives Rajya Sabha the SPECIAL power to authorise Parliament to legislate on a matter in the:

options.option_text: State List, in national interest, by 2/3 majority of members present and voting

questions.explanation: Art 249 — RS can pass a resolution by 2/3 of members PRESENT AND VOTING declaring it 'necessary or expedient in the national interest' for Parliament to legislate on a State List item. Resolution valid for 1 year, renewable. Recognises RS as the chamber representing States. Used 4 times in history. Article 312 — similar 2/3 RS resolution to create new All-India Services. Other unique RS powers — election of Vice-President (Art 66; jointly with Lok Sabha).

questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be done by Rajya Sabha?

options.option_text: Pass a Motion of No-Confidence against the Government

questions.explanation: Motion of No-Confidence is a unique LOK SABHA prerogative — Article 75(3) — Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha. RS cannot move it. Money Bills can also originate ONLY in Lok Sabha. RS CAN — discuss budget (no power to amend), initiate impeachment of President (Art 61), pass any other resolution, vote on Constitution Amendment bills, elect VP. President's impeachment can start in either House.

questions.stem: The 'Quorum' for Rajya Sabha to conduct business is:

options.option_text: 1/10 of total members (=25 if strength is 245)

questions.explanation: Article 100(3) — quorum for either House = 1/10 of total members. RS strength 245 → quorum 25. Lok Sabha strength 543 → quorum 55. Without quorum, the Chairman/Speaker may adjourn the House or suspend until quorum is met. Article 100(2) — Vote in the House is by majority of MEMBERS PRESENT AND VOTING, with the Chairman not voting in the first instance but having a casting vote in case of equality.

questions.stem: The state with the LARGEST representation in Rajya Sabha is:
questions.explanation: Allocation of seats — based on State population (Fourth Schedule of Constitution): UP 31, Maharashtra 19, Tamil Nadu 18, Bihar 16, WB 16, AP 11 + 11 (split with Telangana now), Madhya Pradesh 11, Karnataka 12, Gujarat 11, Rajasthan 10. Smallest — Tripura, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Goa, Arunachal Pradesh — 1 each. UTs without legislatures — no representation. Delhi (3), Puducherry (1).
